mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter predicts weakening consumer and construction demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 6% indicates supply-side disruptions in an otherwise healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate price pass-through and margin expansion.
regime_hint: supply shock in tight labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 2% for three months) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, reducing near-term consumption and investment, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly growth > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for two consecutive months, accompanied by a federal funds rate above 2%, signals a risk of real interest rate increases, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately predicting higher inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts related equities and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
